result.d099Final: SENDS. Plain Enter, single line, no modifier, does send. The key NAME is a harness property, not an app behaviour: harness key "Return" produced a trusted keydown carrying key="" / code="" / keyCode=0 with no newline inserted and defaultPrevented false — an event with no key at all, which no app could act on — while harness key "Enter" arrived as key="Enter", isComposing=false, defaultPrevented=true after bubble, and submitted. I confirmed the guard verbatim on origin/main at the claimed line, OttoChatStream.tsx:1301, and the same file's composer hint at line 2523 states "Enter sends. Shift+Enter starts a new line." Independent server-side corroboration, which the worker did not claim: the DB holds a 7-character USER message (= 谢谢，先到这里) at 12:24:35.544 matching the recorded keypress, an AGENT reply at 12:24:38.408, and an otto-stream RESERVE at 12:24:35.748 — the send is proven in the database, not only in the DOM. SYNTHETIC-KEY CAVEAT, stated as required: this was injected keyboard input through the browser automation harness, not a physical keystroke. The event was isTrusted:true, and the "Return"-vs-"Enter" divergence demonstrates that the harness's key naming, not the app, decided whether an Enter event existed — a real keyboard always emits key="Enter", so the result generalizes. One genuine coverage gap: isComposing was false because text was injected rather than IME-composed, so the guard's third clause (the Chinese-IME composition path) was not exercised despite the message being Chinese. cmd+Enter was correctly not run, since the brief called for it only on failure.
findings: CLOSE R3-F34. Every acceptance leg passes on re-proof, the staging build under test (92193a4d) is the fix commit itself, and the root cause is repaired at its single source (OttoPanel.tsx:400 restores `flex flex-col` to data-otto-panel-body). No leg forces it to stay open.

The fix ships with two fences, so closing does not leave the bug unguarded: a mutation-proven jsdom structural contract (apps/web/lib/__tests__/otto-panel-scroll-chain-r3f34.test.tsx, 4 assertions — the commit records that removing `flex flex-col` turns the first one red and names the broken link) and a real-Chromium journey (e2e/journeys/31-otto-panel-scroll.spec.ts, not skipped, under the required e2e check per the project's merge rules).

ONE COVERAGE NOTE, not a blocker. The fix commit claims three user-visible effects; the third is 打开有长回答的对话直接停在最新一句 (opening a conversation that already holds a long answer lands on the newest line). The staging retest never exercised a genuine fresh page load or conversation open — the nearest proxies are the expand relayout (dfb 0 at open) and the pre-send sample (dfb 0 with a 4,842-char answer already present). That third symptom IS covered by e2e journey 31 ('打开就停在最新一句'), so it is guarded overall, just not re-proven on staging.

THE ZERO-CREDIT BRIEF WAS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN — fix the brief, not the worker. On this build Otto text chat is itself metered (the panel says chatting costs credits; each reply carries a 'This reply used N credits.' footer), so any test that sends an Otto message must spend. The 2.5 credits are the floor cost of the two messages the task required, the reserve/settle pairs are clean and balanced, and the part that actually mattered held: GenJob unchanged at 37, no paid card proposed or approved. Future Otto-chat briefs should say 'no paid generation cards' rather than 'ZERO credits'.

EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE GAP: the group produced no screenshots on disk despite listing seven, and the report's stated reason (the harness cannot write them) is contradicted by a sibling group in the same session directory that saved three PNGs. All four regression legs therefore rest on numbers alone. They are coherent and I uphold them, but the group is one evidence source thinner than it reads.

WORTH A SEPARATE A11Y LOOK (worker's OBS-2, and I agree it is a real signal): across the whole stream no button inside the Otto panel carried any label matching stop/cancel/thinking/generating, so 'is it streaming' was unreadable from the accessibility surface and the worker had to infer progress from text growth. Whatever the app shows while streaming has no accessible name — that hurts screen-reader users and makes future tests fragile.
